text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 Alert: Router tail latency spike detected (eu-west-2). p95 450ms -> 1.9s, p99 2.3s -> 6.8s, sustained for ~6m. Several streaming connections reporting stalls. Triggered paging to oncall.

sam: I'm on this. seeing lots of requests being routed to a small set of backends (hot fanout). streaming stalls visible in traces. opening bridge.

marta: looking at router heatmap now. I see an LB policy rollout (weight bump) around 5145678800 that changed per-shard weights. suspicious.

leon: can you paste the alert query? I want to correlate with ingress egress metrics.

sam: alert link: https://grafana.internal/alerts/5145 (logs and traces attached). Top offending shard ids: 7312, 7313, 7314. throughput normal, but tail latency huge.

marta: those shard ids are in eu-west-2 and got an eager-weight assignment from the new steering policy. I'm rolling that policy rollback in the staging control plane UI now. will patch to revert weights to previous seed.

emily: FYI customer impact: CS reports ~12 customers on streaming sessions seeing stalls/partial responses. Support queue: ~7 tickets flagged as degradations, highest tiers. tagging @support-bot for upstream notifications.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers with template: "We're investigating increased latency for streaming responses in EU; we will update in 30m or when mitigated." Sent to accounts: acme-inc, dataflow-labs, mediawise.

devops: Is there capacity pressure on the backends? VGPU utilization low, but connection queue on a few routers high. might be misrouting rather than infra saturation.

leon: correlating: ingress routing table changes at 5145678798. Router trace shows repeated reroutes causing KV cache churn and cold KV cache reads for decoder states -> large p99.

sam: workaround idea: enable eager-fallback (route to compatible variant with prefix caching) and temporarily scale dedicated pool for eu-west-2 by +20% to reduce pressure. Marta, can we flip eager-fallback flag per-customer or global quickly?

marta: I can toggle eager-fallback at the router config layer. toggling global now (will take ~15s to propagate). also initiating policy rollback as planned.

marta: toggled eager-fallback :white_check_mark: 5145678935 - propagation logs: 
```
POST /api/v1/router/config/flags {"eager_fallback": true}
200 OK
```

leon: seeing immediate drop on connection queue for the hot shards. p95 down to ~700ms, p99 trending down to ~2.8s. good sign.

sam: rolling rollback of LB steering policy to previous seed (5145677722) now. watch for weight rebalancing.

marta: rollback complete :white_check_mark: 5145679001. weights restored. router heatmap shows more uniform distribution now.

emily: support update sent: "We've implemented mitigations (routing fallback + policy rollback). We're monitoring and will follow up with a detailed timeline and root cause analysis." Customers acknowledged.

devops: scaling done: +20% pool capacity in eu-west-2 applied 5145679015. no OOMs or infra errors observed.

leon: p95 now ~230ms, p99 ~380ms. streaming stalls gone from traces. marking as mitigated, but will keep monitoring for another 30m.

sam: starting handoff to night oncall. @marta, please continue to monitor router heatmap and ensure policy rollout jobs are paused until postmortem.

marta: confirms. paused rollout pipeline and reverted the release tag that caused the weight change. will open a postmortem PR with timeline and root cause analysis.

support-bot: Customer update: "Incident mitigated. We applied routing fallback and rolled back a weight change. Root cause under investigation; we'll follow up with details." Sent to impacted accounts.

leon: creating a quick incident note: cause appears to be a bad steering policy rollout that concentrated weight onto a small shard subset (hot partitioning). Side effects: KV cache churn, repeated reroutes, and streaming stalls -> p99 spike. Mitigations: policy rollback, enable eager-fallback, temporary capacity scale.

sam: immediate action items: 
- marta: block that rollout and add preflight heatmap check
- devops: autoscale policy review to allow faster burst capacity for streaming
- leon: add a short-term alert for shard weight skew > 3x
- support-bot: follow up with customers in 2 hours

marta: noted. will include a unit test in rollout pipeline that flags >2x weight variance across shards for a region.

devops: will add an autoscaler emergency path for streaming workloads that can be triggered by oncall with a single command.

leon: will schedule traces + heap of sampled streaming sessions for postmortem.

sam: handing off. I'm leaving the bridge to marta. if anything regresses, escalate to pager and call immediate bridge.

marta: taking over bridge and monitoring. thx all. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. page resolved at 5145679222. Follow-up: postmortem required, severity: P1 -> writeup due EOD.

support-bot: Logged tickets and CCs. template for customer RTFU placed in /docs/incidents/templates/streaming-latency.

sam: closing thread from my side. please add timeline and logs to the postmortem PR so we can run a canary for the rollout change before re-rolling.

marta: will do. PR link (placeholder): https://git.internal/infra/rollout-postmortems/PR-5145

leon: final note: recommend adding a synthetic that simulates hotspot redistribution to catch this earlier. I'll draft a proposal.

emily: thanks everyone. good coordination. :white_check_mark:

marta: assigning follow-ups: infra review, rollout pipeline test, alert tuning. will update once PR done.

support-bot: Incident closed in support triage, customers will get final postmortem once ready.
